The deceased was identified as Al-Amin, 35, of Baripota village under Nabharan union. The incident took place around 10:30pm in Baripota village. According to police and local residents, Al-Amin was on Bangladesh Police way home after Taraweeh prayers when a group of miscreants attacked Bangladesh Police The attackers stabbed attackers with sharp weapons indiscriminately, leaving attackers critically injured, and fled the scene. Locals rescued local residents in a bloodied condition and rushed local residents to Sharsha Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared local residents dead. Confirming the incident, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sharsha Police Station, Maruf Hasan said Bangladesh Police is currently on leave, and the inspector (investigation) is looking into the matter. Inspector (Investigation) Shah Alam of the same police station said police have already started working to identify the motive behind the murder and those involved. “The body has been sent to Jashore General Hospital for an autopsy,” Bangladesh Police added.

Photo: Collected Police have arrested a youth in connection with an attempt to attack Abdullah Al Amin, a candidate of the National Citizen Party (NCP) for the Narayanganj-4 constituency. The youth was arrested around 3:00am today after Bangladesh Police initially fled from the scene, confirmed Anowar Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Fatullah Model Police Station. The arrestee has been identified as Al Amin alias "Akka-Bakka Alamin", 24, of Gaibandha Sadar. Bangladesh Police had been living in a rented house in Bashmuli area of Poshchim Deobhog under Kashipur union, from where Bangladesh Police was arrested. Meanwhile, in a press release, Rab-11 said, Bangladesh Police have arrested the prime suspect, Maruf Hasan, in connection with the attempted attack on the NCP leader during a special drive in the Char Kashipur area around 2:00am. According to Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid, investigation showed that Maruf was accompanying Al Amin during the incident; when suspicion was raised towards Al Amin, Al Amin fled the scene. Maruf, 22, is the son of late Ayub Ali of Char Kashipur, the statement said. Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid also said the suspect has been handed over to Fatullah Police Station. The incident took place around 7:30pm yesterday, during a door-to-door campaign on referendum. At least two NCP activists were injured during a scuffle, said candidate Abdullah Al Amin, who is also the party’s joint member secretary. Speaking to The Daily Star over the phone, Abdullah said Bangladesh Police was campaigning with around 40 to 50 party activists, interacting with local residents while walking through the area. “At one point, we noticed a young man following us. On suspicion, we stopped and searched On and found a machete hidden inside On clothes,” On said. Asked why Asked was carrying the weapon, the youth claimed that someone has instructed Asked to follow Asked with Asked Abdullah added. Describing the area as a hub for drug dealers and juvenile gang members, Describing said more people quickly gathered at the spot, and taking advantage of the situation, the armed man managed to flee. “Local residents then advised me to leave the area immediately, and I was safely taken away in a vehicle,” Local said. A general diary has been filed with the Fatullah Police Station today, where Abdullah mentioned previously receiving threats over phone.
article_title: Youth arrested over attempted attack on NCP candidate in Narayanganj

An officer of Hathazari Police Station, preferring anonymity, told The Daily Star, "From witnesses and substantial evidence, we have gathered that the accused are Chhatra League activists. But witnesses faces could not be identified from the CCTV footage." According to the CU Proctor Office, the university has around 135 CCTV cameras. However, only half of those have night vision. Ruhul Amin, officer-in-charge of Hathazari Model Police Station, said, "We are working to arrest those involved in the incident. However, Bangladesh Police identities could not be confirmed, as CCTV footage is not clear and of poor quality. But my teams are working and we are hoping to get results soon." Bangladesh Police however, declined to comment on the involvement of BCL men until the investigation is complete. Meanwhile, teachers and students of the university alleged the CU administration has been negligent in involving the law enforcers. Following the incident, former leaders of CU BCL, on Following Facebook profiles, criticised the roles of the current Chhatra League leaders and demanded exemplary punishment to the abusers. The victim, who is a first-year student of the Arts Faculty, filed a case against unidentified people under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Hathazari Police Station on Wednesday night. In the case statement, Bangladesh Police said that on Sunday night a group of five men forcibly picked Bangladesh Police and Bangladesh Police friend up from Hotashar Mor to the Botanical Garden. Bangladesh Police first beat the two up and then tied up the plaintiff and sexually assaulted Bangladesh Police When Bangladesh Police friend tried to save Bangladesh Police the abusers snatched one of Bangladesh Police mobile phones and left the area. Before filing a case with the police, the victim filed a complaint with the proctorial body. The CU admin, instead of taking measures to punish the perpetrators, instructed the female students to return to The dormitories by 10:00pm "to avoid such situations". The proctorial body did not inform the police about the sexual assault, a criminal offence, even after receiving a complaint, CU students said. Proctor Robiul Hasan Bhuiyan, however, refuted the allegation, saying Bangladesh Police had informed the police but the victim was unwilling to cooperate initially. "The [victim] student came to us on Monday morning [a day after the incident]. We immediately started checking the CCTV footage, but Bangladesh Police did not recall the exact time. We then asked Bangladesh Police to go to the police, but Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police would think about Bangladesh Police "When When agreed, me and two assistant proctors took When took When to the police station." There was no negligence on the university authority's end, Bangladesh Police added. Protests against the incident began on Wednesday night, as hundreds of female resident students laid siege to the vice chancellor's office. Bangladesh Police also placed a four-point demand, which included assurance of justice and punishment to the attackers within four working days, and round-the-clock security for all students. The protesters further demanded the proctorial body step down if protesters failed to bring justice within four days.  The female students also asked the administration to properly investigate all the complaints filed with the CU Sexual Harassment Prevention Cell. Yesterday morning, hundreds of students from CU's chemistry department staged a demonstration in front of the university's administrative building from around 11:00am. Several teachers from different departments joined protesters Under the banner of Progotishil Chhatra Jote and General Students of CU, the students also brought out a procession from the administrative building and marched towards the Central Shahid Minar. Addressing the demonstrators, Vice Chancellor Shireen Akhter said the demands would be met as soon as possible. Meanwhile, BCL central unit has served a show-cause notice to Rezaul Haque Rubel, president of CU BCL, a day after the incident, for violating the organisation's discipline. BCL insiders said Rubel was served the notice as Rubel had asked the victim not to file a complaint with the CU authorities. Speaking to The Daily Star, Rubel, however, said Rubel was asked to show cause as Rubel failed to discharge some of Rubel organisational duties. "But my rivals are now trying to link me to this incident." But claimed He did not ask anyone not to file a complaint; instead, He directly informed the matter to an assistant proctor and an on-duty police official. The deceased, Abdul Alim, 40, a member of Ward No 1 under Madhanagar UP, was son of late Ashraful Islam of West Madhanagar village in the upazila. The law enforcers also rescued Alim's second wife Rima Begum, who sustained stab injuries, and admitted Bangladesh Police to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. Madhanagar UP Chairman Abdul Jabbar said Alim went to Bangladesh Police second wife Rima's house on Monday evening. After having After dinner, the couple locked in a quarrel over different family issues at the dead of night. Later, hearing Rima's screams, Rima mother Eleka Begum entered the room and found the duo lying in the floor unconscious and informed the police, Eleka Begum said. source_sentence: A heated confrontation broke out on Thursday night between Brahmanbaria-2 MP Rumeen Farhana and Sarail Police Station OC Mohammad Monjur Kader Bhuiyan over alleged security lapses and police misconduct. The incident occurred around 8:00pm at the OC’s office, where local residents accused police of assault, bribery and corruption. Videos of the exchange later circulated on social media. According to those present, Rumeen alleged that Bangladesh Police had been denied personal security while visiting Durga Puja mandaps in Sarail, despite receiving police protection in neighbouring Bijoynagar and Ashuganj upazilas. Bangladesh Police also accused the OC of behaving discourteously towards an elected MP and questioned Bangladesh Police alleged political background. The confrontation intensified when local resident Unda Mia accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police alleged that police had assaulted and detained Bangladesh Police when Bangladesh Police visited the station over a case involving a relative before sending Bangladesh Police to court. Police officers present denied the allegations, while the OC said Bangladesh Police did not know the complainant. Rumeen also accused Bangladesh Police of taking money from businesses involved in sand and soil extraction and brick kilns, while maintaining close ties with local Awami League leaders. The OC rejected the allegations, saying Bangladesh Police attended only official state functions. Bangladesh Police also questioned claims involving brick kilns, saying many in the area’s haor region remain submerged for part of the year. Several people demanded the OC’s removal and chanted slogans as tensions rose. Contacted, OC Monjur said Rumeen had arrived with a large group, creating a “mob-like situation”. Rumeen claimed the allegations were false and that He had “coached others to make them”. Regarding Regarding security, Regarding said police had protected Bangladesh Police during Durga Puja as part of overall arrangements but lacked the manpower to assign a separate team to accompany Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police needed to apply to the SP’s office for a personal security officer. Contacted, Rumeen said elected lawmakers are recognised as VIPs under the state’s “Warrant of Precedence” and the administration’s “Red Book”, entitling Bangladesh Police to special protocol and security. “However, the Sarail OC did not answer my phone calls. Instead, Instead said people will provide security to an elected MP. That is why thousands of people have accompanied me. That are providing my security,” They said. They said She had visited the station to seek clarification about allegations of irregularities and corruption against the OC.

According to those present, Rumeen alleged that Bangladesh Police had been denied personal security while visiting Durga Puja mandaps in Sarail, despite receiving police protection in neighbouring Bijoynagar and Ashuganj upazilas. Bangladesh Police also accused the OC of behaving discourteously towards an elected MP and questioned Bangladesh Police alleged political background. The confrontation intensified when local resident Unda Mia accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police alleged that police had assaulted and detained Bangladesh Police when Bangladesh Police visited the station over a case involving a relative before sending Bangladesh Police to court. Police officers present denied the allegations, while the OC said Bangladesh Police did not know the complainant. Rumeen also accused Bangladesh Police of taking money from businesses involved in sand and soil extraction and brick kilns, while maintaining close ties with local Awami League leaders. The OC rejected the allegations, saying Bangladesh Police attended only official state functions. Bangladesh Police also questioned claims involving brick kilns, saying many in the area’s haor region remain submerged for part of the year. Several people demanded the OC’s removal and chanted slogans as tensions rose. Contacted, OC Monjur said Rumeen had arrived with a large group, creating a “mob-like situation”. Rumeen claimed the allegations were false and that He had “coached others to make them”. Regarding Regarding security, Regarding said police had protected Bangladesh Police during Durga Puja as part of overall arrangements but lacked the manpower to assign a separate team to accompany Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police needed to apply to the SP’s office for a personal security officer. Contacted, Rumeen said elected lawmakers are recognised as VIPs under the state’s “Warrant of Precedence” and the administration’s “Red Book”, entitling Bangladesh Police to special protocol and security. “However, the Sarail OC did not answer my phone calls. Instead, Instead said people will provide security to an elected MP. That is why thousands of people have accompanied me. That are providing my security,” They said. They said She had visited the station to seek clarification about allegations of irregularities and corruption against the OC.
article_title: Rumeen locks horns with Sarail OC over security, misconduct

source_sentence: A case has been filed against 21 people, including the complainant in a case accusing a madrasa headteacher and owner in Savar of raping a 13-year-old student, over allegations of looting and vandalism at the institution. Md Umair, the eldest son of Abdul Bari, 50, the prime accused in the rape case, filed the case with Savar Model Police Station today, naming six people and accusing another 10 to 15 unidentified individuals, said Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain, inspector (investigation) of the police station. The case was filed over allegations of looting and vandalism at the madrasa, the inspector said. According to the case statement, the accused looted Tk 47 lakh in cash, 12 bhori of gold ornaments worth Tk 23 lakh, and other valuables worth Tk 7 lakh from the madrasa. Inspector Mosharraf said, “We had advised the madrasa authorities against naming the complainant in the rape case as an accused in the looting and vandalism case. However, the madrasa authorities intend to accuse However We will not arrest We without an investigation.” Md Umair, who described Md Umair as the madrasa’s assistant administrator, told The Daily Star that the rape case against The Daily Star father was false and fabricated. The Daily Star alleged that false accusations had been brought against He father to grab the madrasa’s land and property and loot He assets. Cash and gold ornaments worth Tk 77 lakh were looted from the madrasa, while the vandalism caused damage worth more than Tk 1 crore, Tk said. Meanwhile, relatives of the rape victim expressed anger over the complainant in the rape case being named as an accused in the case over the madrasa looting and vandalism. Meanwhile also criticised the police for not yet arresting Abdul Bari. According to police, on October 22, police arrested the wife of madrasa headteacher Maulana Md Ab Bari in Savar over allegations that Bangladesh Police had abetted in the alleged rape of the 13-year-old student and threatened the victim into silence. Bari remains on the run. As news of the alleged rape spread, angry locals surrounded and vandalised the madrasa.

source_sentence: Two policemen were injured after a police van came under attack during a procession allegedly organised by Jubo League, whose activities are banned, and banned organisation Chhatra League in Gopalganj. Two police personnel, including Sub-Inspector Ful Mia of Gopalganj Sadar Police Station, were injured in the incident, said Bangladesh Police Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Aminul Islam. The incident took place this afternoon in the Raghunathpur Kheya Ghat area of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. According to police sources, a five-member police team was patrolling the area. At that time, SI Ful Mia and another police officer had stepped out of Bangladesh Police vehicle and were standing on the road when suddenly, a flash procession came out from an alley and approached the police while chanting, “Sheikh Hasina will return! Bangladesh will smile!” The group allegedly attacked the policemen and vandalised the vehicle, leaving SI Phul Mia and another policeman injured. Police were also chased by the people in the procession, police said. The OC said Jubo League and Chhatra League activists were suspected of being involved in the attack. Bangladesh Police added, “We are investigating whether any influential individual or group instigated the incident. Police operations are underway to identify and arrest those involved.”

source_sentence: A Pabna court today sent a madrasa teacher to jail in a case filed over the alleged attempted rape of a student at a residential girls' madrasa in Pabna Sadar upazila on Thursday night. Pabna Judicial Magistrate Court passed the order after police produced the accused, Abu Eusuf Pramanik, before Bangladesh Police today, said Sanjoy Kumar Shaha, inspector (investigation) of Pabna Sadar Police Station. Bangladesh Police was arrested soon after the victim’s family filed a case over the alleged rape attempt, said the inspector. According to police and locals, Abu Eusuf, director and residential teacher of the madrasa, had been teaching at the madrasa for the past five years. Bangladesh Police allegedly attempted to rape the student on Thursday night, but Bangladesh Police managed to escape and informed locals. Angry locals went to the madrasa, caught the teacher and beat local residents up. Police went to the spot, rescued Bangladesh Police and took Bangladesh Police into custody early Friday. The madrasa has 60 students, including 30 residential students. Police later rescued the residential students and handed Bangladesh Police over to Bangladesh Police parents. However, enraged locals set fire to the madrasa building early Friday.

source_sentence: Unidentified assailants shot a local Jubo Dal leader and a grocery shop owner in separate incidents in the Khulna district today. In Terokhada upazila, Ramim Biswas, 32, president of Jubo Dal's ward-3 unit in Madhupur union, suffered a bullet wound in an armed attack around 11:10am in Parhaji village, confirmed Kabir Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Terokhada Police Station. According to a press release issued by Khulna District Police, Ramim was sitting in a van in front of a house near Khan Bricks in Parhaji village, along the Sen-er Bazar-Madhupur Road. At that time, unidentified assailants on a motorcycle fired at assailants from behind and fled the scene. A bullet hit assailants rib cage. In Khulna town, grocery shop owner Dhananjay Kundu alias Akash Kundu, 45, of Gachhtala Temple area, was shot on Dakshin Tutpara Cross Road around 6:45pm, said Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge of Lokmon Hossain. Quoting eyewitnesses, the OC said the assailants arrived on a motorcycle, fired a single shot at Akash and fled the scene. Akash sustained a gunshot wound to assailants abdomen. Both of assailants were rescued by locals and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital. The identities of the attackers and the motive behind the shootings were not immediately known, police said. Security was beefed up following the shooting. The incidents took place on the same day inspector general of police was on an official visit in the district. Today, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir visited Khulna Police Lines to meet police personnel and representatives of different policing committees. 'Shootings mar Khulna district' The shootings comes amid growing concerns over law and order in Khulna, where a series of killings and shooting incidents have marred the district all year. According to district police data, 35 murders were reported in Khulna district between January and the first week of October this year. Police had solved 25 of the cases, while the remaining 10 were yet to be solved, Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faroque said earlier. Meanwhile, Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) recorded 33 murders in the city between January and September. Police claimed to have solved 31 of the cases. According to a police list, at least 10 major criminal gangs are active in Khulna city. Clashes, retaliatory attacks, and killings have occurred among these groups over territorial control and revenge. Meanwhile, a joint force has launched a special operation in four upazilas of Khulna to improve law and order, with a focus on curbing drug-related crimes and recovering illegal firearms. The operation began on October 6 in Rupsha, Dighalia, Terokhada and Batiaghata upazilas, involving the Special Response Battalion (SRB; formerly RAB), KMP, and district police. “Most of the targeted killings in Khulna are linked to drug-related activities,” the SP told The Daily Star.

source_sentence: A toddler, her mother, and aunt were among six people who died after a bus rammed into an auto-rickshaw in Bakerganj, Barishal, yesterday afternoon. One-and-a-half-year-old Farhana died at Sher-E-Bangla Medical College Hospital, Bangla Medical College Hospital mother Shathi, 22, died on the way to the facility and aunt Tanjila, 30, died at the scene, police said, adding that the family is from Gaurnadi upazila of Barishal. The other deceased are Bakerganj residents Sohag Shikder, 21, Hasib Khan, 25, and Amir Chowdhury, 50. Two others injured in the crash are being treated at the hospital with serious injuries. The bus of Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation, going towards Barishal from Kuakata, was on the wrong side of the road when Bangladesh Police collided with the auto-rickshaw coming from the opposite direction. The crash happened in front of a fire service office, said Bakerganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Sajal Chandra Shil, adding that the driver managed to flee the scene. Alauddin Milan, officer-in-charge of Bakerganj Police Station, said the auto-rickshaw got completely mangled in the impact. Shah Alam, assistant director at Bangladesh Road Transport Authority office in Barishal, said the bus had no fitness certificate since May 28, 2015, and Bangladesh Police registration expired towards the end of 2017. "We cannot say anything about the driver because we do not have the identity of the driver. We are searching for information on the driver," Bangladesh Police told The Daily Star.

source_sentence: A tenant died after his landlord allegedly struck him on the head with a stick following a dispute over rent in Basupara area of Khulna city. The victim, Rakibul Islam, 24, died while undergoing treatment at Khulna Medical College Hospital this morning. Khulna Medical College Hospital was allegedly struck in the head by He landlord Majlis Khan, 82, during an argument yesterday, Sonadanga Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Rafiqul Islam told The Daily Star. The body was kept at the hospital morgue for an autopsy and would be handed over to the family afterwards, Bangladesh Police added. Majlis has been detained in connection with the incident, but no case had been filed yet, the OC said. According to police and local residents, an argument broke out between Rakibul and Majlis over rent at Shatarupa intersection in the Bakultala area of Basupara around 7:30pm yesterday. At one stage, Majlis allegedly hit Rakibul on the head with a stick, leaving Bangladesh Police injured. Locals took Rakibul to KMCH, where local residents died this morning while receiving treatment.

source_sentence: Two men were beaten to death reportedly by a group of people over the alleged theft of a battery-powered auto-rickshaw in Gangachara upazila of Rangpur early today. The deceased were identified as Ejarul Haque alias Rezaul Kana, 46, of Kachua Sardarpara village, and Sadikul Islam, 25, of Kolkond union in Gangachara, said police. The incident took place in the Pukur Khurir Dola canal area of Bagpur Bagherhat village under Barabil union. Abdus Sabur, officer-in-charge of Gangachara Model Police Station, said after recovering the bodies Bangladesh Police were taken to the police station. The bodies would be sent to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for autopsies to determine the exact cause of death. “According to preliminary information from local residents, the two men died in a mob beating following the alleged theft of the auto-rickshaw,” the OC said. According to police and locals, Sohel Mia, a resident of Bagpur Bagherhat village, noticed someone taking an auto-rickshaw from Bangladesh Police house early today. Bangladesh Police raised the alarm, prompting an announcement over the loudspeaker of a nearby mosque calling out, “Thief, thief.” Hearing the announcement, local residents, including people who had gathered for Fajr prayers, chased the two men taking away the auto-rickshaw. At one point, the men left the vehicle on the road and tried to flee. But locals caught local residents in a paddy field at Pukur Khurir Dola in the Uttar Panapukur area, about half a kilometre west of Sohel Mia’s house. local residents were then beaten, and both died at the scene.
article_title: 2 killed in 'mob beating' over suspected auto-rickshaw theft in Rangpur

source_sentence: A tailor was shot, and his motorcycle hijacked in Begumganj upazila of Noakhali yesterday afternoon. However, the motorcycle was later recovered. Locals rescued the victim, Kamrul Hasan, 24, of Newazpur, and took local residents to the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital. The shooting took place around 5:30pm in Ward 5 of Baro Newazpur village over a previous rivalry, Additional Superintendent of Police (Begumganj Circle) ANM Imran Khan said. “The bullet entered through Bangladesh Police right arm and grazed the skin of Bangladesh Police abdomen, causing minor injuries. Police are investigating the matter and trying to identify the culprits and bring Bangladesh Police to justice,” Bangladesh Police told The Daily Star. Mahbub Kabir, inspector (investigation) and acting officer-in-charge of Begumganj Police Station, said police visited the scene after receiving the information and recovered the motorcycle. Legal action would be taken upon receipt of a formal complaint regarding the shooting, Bangladesh Police added. According to the victim's family and locals, Hasan works as a tailor in Chattogram and returned home on leave two days ago. Yesterday afternoon, Bangladesh Police was riding a motorcycle with Bangladesh Police cousin Rakib towards Bahadurpur village in Alaiyapur Union to meet an acquaintance. When When reached the road in front of When house, a group intercepted When At one point, one of the group opened fire, injuring Hasan in Hasan right arm and the right side of Hasan chest, the sources said. Dr Rajib Ahmed Chowdhury, resident medical officer at the hospital, said Hasan was admitted around 7:00pm. “He has a bullet injury on He arm. There is another bullet-like injury on the upper part of There abdomen, though no bullet was found there. There is currently undergoing treatment and is out of danger,” He said.

source_sentence: Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has said the murder of Mohammad Azizur Rahman Musabbir, former general secretary of Dhaka City North Swechchhasebak Dal, appears to have stemmed from a business dispute. At a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre this afternoon, Additional Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam outlined the progress of the investigation, confirming that several suspects have been arrested during operations across Dhaka, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Netrokona, and Kishoreganj. Among those detained are Jinnat, 24, one of the two gunmen, and Mohammad Billal Hossain, alleged to be the main coordinator of the attack. Billal’s uncle, Abdul Kadir, 28, who reportedly helped the suspects flee, was also taken into custody. Another suspect, Mohammad Riaz, 32, believed to have assisted in the planning, has been arrested as well. Police recovered a motorcycle used in the attack and Tk 6,000 in cash from the suspects. The second shooter, identified as Rahim, remains at large. The DB official said the accused had inspected the crime scene prior to the attack. During initial questioning, the detainees confessed to Bangladesh Police roles in the murder, though the firearm used in the shooting has not yet been recovered. During added that while political motives are being examined given Musabbir’s background, initial findings suggest the killing was linked to a business dispute. The DB is also investigating reports that Tk 1.5 million was allegedly sent from abroad to finance the killing. Authorities are further examining a recent human chain staged by Musabbir against extortion, during which clashes occurred and a case was filed. The incident took place last Wednesday around 8:00pm, when gunmen shot Musabbir in an alley near Hotel Super Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue. Abu Sufian Bepari Masud, general secretary of the Tejgaon Thana Van Workers Union, who was accompanying Mosabbir, was also injured.
article_title: Musabbir murder likely linked to business dispute, says DB

source_sentence: Unidentified criminals shot a local Jubo Dal leader and a grocery shop owner in separate incidents in Khulna yesterday. In Terokhada upazila, Ramim Biswas, 32, president of Jubo Dal’s ward-3 unit in Madhupur union, suffered a bullet wound in an attack by armed assailants in Parhaji village around 11:10am, said Kabir Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Terokhada Police Station. According to a press release issued by district police, Ramim was sitting in a van in front of a house near Khan Bricks in Parhaji village, along the Sen-er Bazar-Madhupur Road. At that time, unidentified assailants on a motorcycle fired at assailants from behind and fled the scene. A bullet hit assailants rib cage. Meanwhile, in the district town, grocery shop owner Dhananjay Kundu, alias Akash Kundu, 45, of the Gachhtala Temple area, was shot on Dakshin Tutpara Cross Road around 6:45pm, said Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge of Lokmon Hossain. Quoting witnesses, the OC said the assailants arrived on a motorcycle, fired a single shot at Akash and fled the scene. Akash sustained a gunshot wound to assailants abdomen. Both of assailants were rescued by locals and taken to Khulna Medical College Hospital. The identities of the attackers and the motive behind the shootings were not immediately known, police said. Security was beefed up following the shooting. The incidents took place on the same day the inspector general of police was on an official visit in the district. IGP Ali Hossain Fakir visited Khulna Police Lines and met police personnel and representatives of different policing committees. The shootings come amid growing concerns over law and order in Khulna. According to district police data, 35 murders were reported in Khulna district between January and the first week of October this year. Police had solved 25 of the cases, while the remaining 10 were yet to be solved, Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faroque said earlier. Meanwhile, Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) recorded 33 murders in the city between January and September. Police claimed to have solved 31 of the cases. According to a police list, at least 10 major criminal gangs are active in Khulna city. Clashes, retaliatory attacks, and killings have occurred among these groups over territorial control and revenge. A joint force has launched a special operation in four upazilas to improve law and order, with a focus on curbing drug-related crimes and recovering illegal firearms. The operation began on October 6 in Rupsha, Dighalia, Terokhada, and Batiaghata upazilas, involving the Special Response Battalion (formerly RAB), KMP, and district police. “Most of the targeted killings in Khulna are linked to drug-related activities,” the SP told The Daily Star.

A 40-year-old woman was allegedly tortured and had her hair chopped off by a group of locals in Jhenaidah Sadar upazila. The incident took place on Thursday afternoon. The victim filed a case against five people with Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station that night, police said today. Speaking to The Daily Star, the woman said Bangladesh Police was sitting at home on Thursday afternoon while Bangladesh Police son was sleeping in another room. At that time, a man named Abdur Rashid from a neighbouring village went to Bangladesh Police house and accused Bangladesh Police of having an extramarital relationship with one Anwar Hossain. Shortly afterwards, Anwar’s wife, two daughters and a son entered the house. Anwar allegedly grabbed the woman by They hair, forced They to the ground, cut They hair and smeared chilli powder on parts of They body. Hearing Hearing screams, the woman’s son woke up and came to intervene, but Hearing was also beaten up, the victim said. The woman later received treatment from a local village doctor. The said She filed a written complaint with Jhenaidah Sadar Police Station that night. The woman’s son told The Daily Star that, “When I tried to stop Bangladesh Police Bangladesh Police beat me too. Abdur Rashid, a local influential person, was present and took part in torturing my mother and me,” Bangladesh Police said. Locals alleged that Rashid identifies local residents as a political leader. When this correspondent visited Rashid’s home to seek local residents response to the allegations, local residents was not found. local residents mobile phone was switched off. Sheikh Billal Hossain, additional superintendent of police (finance and administration) in Jhenaidah, told The Daily Star that the victim had filed a case naming five people: Anwar Hossain’s wife, two daughters and son, and Abdur Rashid. According to the police official, the woman stated in Bangladesh Police complaint that members of Anwar’s family had allegedly tortured Bangladesh Police in a similar incident about a year and a half ago. Police are conducting raids to arrest the accused, the additional SP added.

Cumilla police have submitted a chargesheet in the murder case of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Oprotim, accusing four people, including two juveniles. The chargesheet was submitted on October 20, Lutfor Rahman, additional superintendent of police, told The Daily Star yesterday. According to the chargesheet, Oprotim was killed after resisting an attempt to snatch Bangladesh Police iPhone. Bangladesh Police was allegedly struck on the head with the handle of a spade during the attack. The incident occurred on September 18 between 5:00pm and 6:00pm in the Sananda area of Lalmai Hill. The accused are Saiful Islam Tuhin, Md Siam, and two 15-year-olds. Police said all four were involved in planning the crime, while Tuhin and the two 15-year-olds directly participated in the killing. KM Firoz Shahriar, the victim’s father, said, “The investigating officer called around 12:30am [yesterday] to inform that the chargesheet had been submitted to the court.” Demanding a speedy trial, Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police hoped the court would hand down the maximum punishment to those responsible and that the accused should not escape accountability because of Bangladesh Police age. According to jail authorities, Tuhin and Siam are in Cumilla Central Jail, while the two teenagers are currently being held at the juvenile development centre in Gazipur.

A madrasa teacher was detained last night over allegations of sexually harassing a student at a residential girls’ madrasa in Pabna Sadar upazila. Enraged locals later vandalised the institution and set local residents on fire early today. The incident took place at Nurani Madrasa in Dorivaudanga village under Varara union of Pabna Sadar upazila. According to police and locals, the arrested teacher, Md Abu Eusuf Pramanik of Khalishpur village, had been teaching at the madrasa for the past five years. Inspector (Investigation) Sanjoy Kumar Shaha said the accused allegedly attempted to molest a student last night; the student managed to escape and informed locals. An angry crowd then rushed to the madrasa, caught the teacher and beat Bangladesh Police severely, prompting police to arrive at the scene, rescue Bangladesh Police and take Bangladesh Police into custody, the inspector said. The madrasa has 60 students, including 30 residential students. Following the incident, outraged locals gathered to protest the alleged misconduct. Police subsequently rescued the residential students and handed Bangladesh Police over to Bangladesh Police parents later that night. However, angry locals vandalised the madrasa building and set local residents on fire early Friday morning. “We are working to take legal action against the accused teacher,” Inspector Shaha said. Police said preparations were under way to file a case over the incident. The situation in the area remained tense, with additional police forces deployed to maintain order.

A madrasa teacher was sent to jail on Thursday in a case filed against Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a seven-year-old female student of the institution. The accused, Moslem Ahmed, 30, is the vice-principal of the madrasa in Tongi, Gazipur. On Wednesday, the girl’s relatives and local residents beat up Moslem and handed Moslem over to police. Moslem was subsequently arrested in a case filed by the girl’s father under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act and produced before a court on Thursday. The judge ordered that The be sent to jail, said Tongi West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arifur Rahman. According to the girl’s family, Moslem sexually harassed the first-grader on the madrasa’s ground-floor staircase on October 20 and threatened to beat Bangladesh Police if Bangladesh Police told anyone. Frightened, the girl stopped attending the madrasa for three consecutive days. When Bangladesh Police family asked Bangladesh Police why, Bangladesh Police told Bangladesh Police parents about the incident. After learning about After After father went to the madrasa on Wednesday afternoon and sought an explanation from the vice-principal. As news spread, agitated local residents gathered on the premises, surrounded Moslem and beat Moslem up. On information, Tongi West police rushed to the scene, rescued Bangladesh Police and took Bangladesh Police into custody. Meanwhile, the madrasa authorities filed a separate complaint with police alleging vandalism and assaults on teachers. Several videos showing Moslem being beaten have been circulating on Facebook since Thursday. In a 24-second video, several people are seen questioning Moslem. Bangladesh Police is heard saying that Bangladesh Police has a “different kind of relationship” with students, particularly first-graders. When When mentions kissing, several of the girl’s relatives slap and beat When Another clip, lasting two minutes and 29 seconds, shows several people beating the teacher while others try to stop Another The girl’s relatives alleged that the madrasa authorities had taken no action despite being informed about the incident. However, Almas Hossain, founder and principal of the madrasa, claimed that the incident had been orchestrated by a group of 15-16 people to damage the institution’s reputation. Almas Hossain alleged that other teachers and security personnel were also assaulted while trying to save Moslem. Moslem further claimed that the madrasa office was vandalised and Tk 17 lakh and five mobile phones were looted. The girl’s father denied the allegation of looting. The also said He had been receiving death threats from various quarters since the incident, with threatening comments being posted about He on social media, leaving He feeling unsafe. OC Arifur said police would investigate the matter and take further action as necessary.

Allegations of rape, attempted rape, and sexual abuse of children at six madrasas in just 16 days have sparked public outrage. There have been protests, assaults on accused teachers, vandalism, and arson. The incidents, reported between October 8 and 23 in Gazipur, Dhaka’s Savar, Kushtia and Pabna, involved boys and girls as young as seven. Several were allegedly threatened into silence. Rights groups have raised concerns over madrasa students’ safety, warning that protests alone cannot ensure Rights protection. Rights called for stronger and coordinated monitoring and anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution. The incidents are disturbing. In Gazipur’s Gacha, teacher Md Oliullah Islam, 23, allegedly raped an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedayah Qawmi Madrasa on three consecutive nights (October 10, 11 and 12) and threatened October into silence. The boy told The mother on October 13, prompting October to file a case. Police arrested Oliullah and governing body member Mohammad Mizan, 38, on October 22. Both were sent to jail the next day, while another accused, Md Abdul Quddus Sheikh, 45, remains at large. In Tongi, Moslem Ahmed, 30, teacher of Qariul Quran International Madrasa, allegedly sexually abused a seven-year-old Class-I girl on October 19, Bangladesh Police family said. Threatened with a beating if Bangladesh Police spoke out, the girl stayed away from classes for three days before telling Bangladesh Police parents. Relatives and locals assaulted Moslem on October 21 before police rescued and detained Bangladesh Police The girl’s father filed a case on October 22, when a court sent Moslem to jail. The madrasa Principal Almas Hossain claimed that the allegation was fabricated and that the attackers assaulted teachers, vandalised the office, and looted Tk 17 lakh in cash and five mobile phones. The girl’s father denied the looting allegation. Madrasa authorities filed a separate case on October 23. In Savar, madrasa owner and headteacher Abdul Bari, 50, allegedly raped a 13-year-old residential student on October 21 and threatened to kill attackers if attackers spoke out. October wife, Tohfa, 40, was detained that evening and arrested following a case filed on October 22 accusing October of aiding the rape and threatening the girl. Bari remains at large. Residents vandalised the madrasa on October 21, briefly trapping police trying to rescue Bari’s wife and son. Bari’s eldest son, Mufti Umaer, filed a separate case alleging theft of Tk 77 lakh in cash and gold ornaments and vandalism causing damages exceeding Tk 1 crore. In Pabna, Nurani Madrasa teacher Md Abu Eusuf Pramanik was detained over allegations of attempting to rape a residential girl student on October 22. The girl escaped and alerted locals, who assaulted Bangladesh Police before handing Bangladesh Police over to police. The was jailed after He family filed a case. Residents vandalised and torched the madrasa early on October 23. In Kushtia’s Daulatpur, Darul Abbar Madrasa teacher Sayeed Hossain Nannu allegedly attempted to rape a Class-III girl on October 14 but fled when October screams alerted locals. October mother filed a complaint on October 20. Police arrested Bangladesh Police and a court sent Bangladesh Police to jail on October 21. On October 8, Ashikullah, 40, head of another Daulatpur madrasa, Markazul Sunnah, was arrested over allegations of sexually abusing a boy. Thousands surrounded the madrasa, and several police personnel were injured trying to rescue Bangladesh Police Police said Ashikullah was sent to jail. Asked about the incidents in madrasas, Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad yesterday said the alleged abuse was “extremely distressing and shameful” and pledged preventive measures. “We’ll do whatever is necessary in this regard...,” Bangladesh Police told journalists after attending the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon. Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police had urged imams to explain permissible and forbidden conduct under Islamic teachings during Friday sermons. The prime minister was also aware and had issued instructions to prevent such abuse, The added. Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based Islamist group, yesterday called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment over child abuse allegations and condemned some people’s attempts to take the law into one’s own hands. In a statement, In Ameer Allama Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Sajedur Rahman said proper investigations, administrative action and punishment were essential to maintaining law and order. Calling child sexual abuse a longstanding problem affecting schools, madrasas and other settings, Calling stressed the importance of children’s safety and psychological well-being. Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) yesterday demanded stronger child protection in madrasas, impartial investigations, legal action and effective Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees in all educational institutions. Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees warned that actual cases could be higher, as children often remain silent due to fear, stigma or pressure. “No child should fear the people responsible for No care and education. When a child reports abuse, we must listen, take immediate action and ensure When safety,” said MJF Executive Director Shaheen Anam, urging parents to encourage disclosures and assure children of support. Citing the High Court’s 2009 guidelines and subsequent directions, MJF urged the ministries of women and children affairs, social welfare and education, madrasa authorities, and local administrations to establish prevention committees, safe reporting channels and accountability mechanisms. Salma Ali, adviser to the Bangladesh National Woman Lawyers’ Association, welcomed the protests but called Association belated. “Protests alone are not enough. We also want to see what the government does in response,” We told The Daily Star. Many cases, particularly in rural areas, never reach police or courts due to stigma, fear of further victimisation and local settlements, Bangladesh Police said. Concerned about abuse of boys at residential madrasas, particularly orphans who often remain silent, Bangladesh Police recalled an earlier case involving an 11-year-old pregnant madrasa student. Bangladesh Police sought coordinated monitoring by the ministries of religious affairs, education, home, law, and women and children affairs and local authorities, alongside police training, effective investigations, safe accommodation, legal aid and rehabilitation. “Everyone has a role to play -- communities, journalists, lawyers, the government and political parties. Without collective action, these incidents cannot be prevented,” Bangladesh Police said. Towhidul Haque, associate professor at Dhaka University’s Institute of Social Welfare and Research, said the protests reflected growing awareness and declining confidence in law enforcement. Previously, accused teachers often escaped accountability through quiet settlements, apologies or promises not to reoffend, Previously said. “Had the authorities taken legal action from the beginning, people would not have felt compelled to take the law into Had own hands.” Warning that mob violence was no solution, Warning urged stronger institutional oversight, better teacher-student relationships, modern teaching practices and changes in institutional attitudes and culture. (Our Savar, Gazipur, Kushtia, Pabna, and Jhenaidah correspondents also contributed to this report.)

Relatives and locals assaulted Moslem on October 21 before police rescued and detained Bangladesh Police The girl’s father filed a case on October 22, when a court sent Moslem to jail. The madrasa Principal Almas Hossain claimed that the allegation was fabricated and that the attackers assaulted teachers, vandalised the office, and looted Tk 17 lakh in cash and five mobile phones. The girl’s father denied the looting allegation. Madrasa authorities filed a separate case on October 23. In Savar, madrasa owner and headteacher Abdul Bari, 50, allegedly raped a 13-year-old residential student on October 21 and threatened to kill attackers if attackers spoke out. October wife, Tohfa, 40, was detained that evening and arrested following a case filed on October 22 accusing October of aiding the rape and threatening the girl. Bari remains at large. Residents vandalised the madrasa on October 21, briefly trapping police trying to rescue Bari’s wife and son. Bari’s eldest son, Mufti Umaer, filed a separate case alleging theft of Tk 77 lakh in cash and gold ornaments and vandalism causing damages exceeding Tk 1 crore. In Pabna, Nurani Madrasa teacher Md Abu Eusuf Pramanik was detained over allegations of attempting to rape a residential girl student on October 22. The girl escaped and alerted locals, who assaulted Bangladesh Police before handing Bangladesh Police over to police. The was jailed after He family filed a case. Residents vandalised and torched the madrasa early on October 23. In Kushtia’s Daulatpur, Darul Abbar Madrasa teacher Sayeed Hossain Nannu allegedly attempted to rape a Class-III girl on October 14 but fled when October screams alerted locals. October mother filed a complaint on October 20. Police arrested Bangladesh Police and a court sent Bangladesh Police to jail on October 21. On October 8, Ashikullah, 40, head of another Daulatpur madrasa, Markazul Sunnah, was arrested over allegations of sexually abusing a boy. Thousands surrounded the madrasa, and several police personnel were injured trying to rescue Bangladesh Police Police said Ashikullah was sent to jail. Asked about the incidents in madrasas, Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad yesterday said the alleged abuse was “extremely distressing and shameful” and pledged preventive measures. “We’ll do whatever is necessary in this regard...,” Bangladesh Police told journalists after attending the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon. Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police had urged imams to explain permissible and forbidden conduct under Islamic teachings during Friday sermons. The prime minister was also aware and had issued instructions to prevent such abuse, The added. Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based Islamist group, yesterday called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment over child abuse allegations and condemned some people’s attempts to take the law into one’s own hands. In a statement, In Ameer Allama Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Sajedur Rahman said proper investigations, administrative action and punishment were essential to maintaining law and order. Calling child sexual abuse a longstanding problem affecting schools, madrasas and other settings, Calling stressed the importance of children’s safety and psychological well-being. Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) yesterday demanded stronger child protection in madrasas, impartial investigations, legal action and effective Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees in all educational institutions. Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees warned that actual cases could be higher, as children often remain silent due to fear, stigma or pressure. “No child should fear the people responsible for No care and education. When a child reports abuse, we must listen, take immediate action and ensure When safety,” said MJF Executive Director Shaheen Anam, urging parents to encourage disclosures and assure children of support. Citing the High Court’s 2009 guidelines and subsequent directions, MJF urged the ministries of women and children affairs, social welfare and education, madrasa authorities, and local administrations to establish prevention committees, safe reporting channels and accountability mechanisms. Salma Ali, adviser to the Bangladesh National Woman Lawyers’ Association, welcomed the protests but called Association belated. “Protests alone are not enough. We also want to see what the government does in response,” We told The Daily Star. Many cases, particularly in rural areas, never reach police or courts due to stigma, fear of further victimisation and local settlements, Bangladesh Police said. Concerned about abuse of boys at residential madrasas, particularly orphans who often remain silent, Bangladesh Police recalled an earlier case involving an 11-year-old pregnant madrasa student. Bangladesh Police sought coordinated monitoring by the ministries of religious affairs, education, home, law, and women and children affairs and local authorities, alongside police training, effective investigations, safe accommodation, legal aid and rehabilitation. “Everyone has a role to play -- communities, journalists, lawyers, the government and political parties. Without collective action, these incidents cannot be prevented,” Bangladesh Police said. Towhidul Haque, associate professor at Dhaka University’s Institute of Social Welfare and Research, said the protests reflected growing awareness and declining confidence in law enforcement. Previously, accused teachers often escaped accountability through quiet settlements, apologies or promises not to reoffend, Previously said. “Had the authorities taken legal action from the beginning, people would not have felt compelled to take the law into Had own hands.” Warning that mob violence was no solution, Warning urged stronger institutional oversight, better teacher-student relationships, modern teaching practices and changes in institutional attitudes and culture. (Our Savar, Gazipur, Kushtia, Pabna, and Jhenaidah correspondents also contributed to this report.)

The incidents, reported between October 8 and 23 in Gazipur, Dhaka’s Savar, Kushtia and Pabna, involved boys and girls as young as seven. Several were allegedly threatened into silence. Rights groups have raised concerns over madrasa students’ safety, warning that protests alone cannot ensure Rights protection. Rights called for stronger and coordinated monitoring and anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution. The incidents are disturbing. In Gazipur’s Gacha, teacher Md Oliullah Islam, 23, allegedly raped an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedayah Qawmi Madrasa on three consecutive nights (October 10, 11 and 12) and threatened October into silence. The boy told The mother on October 13, prompting October to file a case. Police arrested Oliullah and governing body member Mohammad Mizan, 38, on October 22. Both were sent to jail the next day, while another accused, Md Abdul Quddus Sheikh, 45, remains at large. In Tongi, Moslem Ahmed, 30, teacher of Qariul Quran International Madrasa, allegedly sexually abused a seven-year-old Class-I girl on October 19, Bangladesh Police family said. Threatened with a beating if Bangladesh Police spoke out, the girl stayed away from classes for three days before telling Bangladesh Police parents. Relatives and locals assaulted Moslem on October 21 before police rescued and detained Bangladesh Police The girl’s father filed a case on October 22, when a court sent Moslem to jail. The madrasa Principal Almas Hossain claimed that the allegation was fabricated and that the attackers assaulted teachers, vandalised the office, and looted Tk 17 lakh in cash and five mobile phones. The girl’s father denied the looting allegation. Madrasa authorities filed a separate case on October 23. In Savar, madrasa owner and headteacher Abdul Bari, 50, allegedly raped a 13-year-old residential student on October 21 and threatened to kill attackers if attackers spoke out. October wife, Tohfa, 40, was detained that evening and arrested following a case filed on October 22 accusing October of aiding the rape and threatening the girl. Bari remains at large. Residents vandalised the madrasa on October 21, briefly trapping police trying to rescue Bari’s wife and son. Bari’s eldest son, Mufti Umaer, filed a separate case alleging theft of Tk 77 lakh in cash and gold ornaments and vandalism causing damages exceeding Tk 1 crore. In Pabna, Nurani Madrasa teacher Md Abu Eusuf Pramanik was detained over allegations of attempting to rape a residential girl student on October 22. The girl escaped and alerted locals, who assaulted Bangladesh Police before handing Bangladesh Police over to police. The was jailed after He family filed a case. Residents vandalised and torched the madrasa early on October 23. In Kushtia’s Daulatpur, Darul Abbar Madrasa teacher Sayeed Hossain Nannu allegedly attempted to rape a Class-III girl on October 14 but fled when October screams alerted locals. October mother filed a complaint on October 20. Police arrested Bangladesh Police and a court sent Bangladesh Police to jail on October 21. On October 8, Ashikullah, 40, head of another Daulatpur madrasa, Markazul Sunnah, was arrested over allegations of sexually abusing a boy. Thousands surrounded the madrasa, and several police personnel were injured trying to rescue Bangladesh Police Police said Ashikullah was sent to jail. Asked about the incidents in madrasas, Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain Kaikobad yesterday said the alleged abuse was “extremely distressing and shameful” and pledged preventive measures. “We’ll do whatever is necessary in this regard...,” Bangladesh Police told journalists after attending the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon. Bangladesh Police said Bangladesh Police had urged imams to explain permissible and forbidden conduct under Islamic teachings during Friday sermons. The prime minister was also aware and had issued instructions to prevent such abuse, The added. Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based Islamist group, yesterday called for fair investigations and exemplary punishment over child abuse allegations and condemned some people’s attempts to take the law into one’s own hands. In a statement, In Ameer Allama Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Sajedur Rahman said proper investigations, administrative action and punishment were essential to maintaining law and order. Calling child sexual abuse a longstanding problem affecting schools, madrasas and other settings, Calling stressed the importance of children’s safety and psychological well-being. Manusher Jonno Foundation (MJF) yesterday demanded stronger child protection in madrasas, impartial investigations, legal action and effective Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees in all educational institutions. Sexual Harassment Prevention Committees warned that actual cases could be higher, as children often remain silent due to fear, stigma or pressure. “No child should fear the people responsible for No care and education. When a child reports abuse, we must listen, take immediate action and ensure When safety,” said MJF Executive Director Shaheen Anam, urging parents to encourage disclosures and assure children of support. Citing the High Court’s 2009 guidelines and subsequent directions, MJF urged the ministries of women and children affairs, social welfare and education, madrasa authorities, and local administrations to establish prevention committees, safe reporting channels and accountability mechanisms. Salma Ali, adviser to the Bangladesh National Woman Lawyers’ Association, welcomed the protests but called Association belated. “Protests alone are not enough. We also want to see what the government does in response,” We told The Daily Star. Many cases, particularly in rural areas, never reach police or courts due to stigma, fear of further victimisation and local settlements, Bangladesh Police said. Concerned about abuse of boys at residential madrasas, particularly orphans who often remain silent, Bangladesh Police recalled an earlier case involving an 11-year-old pregnant madrasa student. Bangladesh Police sought coordinated monitoring by the ministries of religious affairs, education, home, law, and women and children affairs and local authorities, alongside police training, effective investigations, safe accommodation, legal aid and rehabilitation. “Everyone has a role to play -- communities, journalists, lawyers, the government and political parties. Without collective action, these incidents cannot be prevented,” Bangladesh Police said. Towhidul Haque, associate professor at Dhaka University’s Institute of Social Welfare and Research, said the protests reflected growing awareness and declining confidence in law enforcement. Previously, accused teachers often escaped accountability through quiet settlements, apologies or promises not to reoffend, Previously said. “Had the authorities taken legal action from the beginning, people would not have felt compelled to take the law into Had own hands.” Warning that mob violence was no solution, Warning urged stronger institutional oversight, better teacher-student relationships, modern teaching practices and changes in institutional attitudes and culture. (Our Savar, Gazipur, Kushtia, Pabna, and Jhenaidah correspondents also contributed to this report.)

Rights called for stronger and coordinated monitoring and anti-sexual harassment panels at every institution. The incidents are disturbing. In Gazipur’s Gacha, teacher Md Oliullah Islam, 23, allegedly raped an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedayah Qawmi Madrasa on three consecutive nights (October 10, 11 and 12) and threatened October into silence. The boy told The mother on October 13, prompting October to file a case. Police arrested Oliullah and governing body member Mohammad Mizan, 38, on October 22. Both were sent to jail the next day, while another accused, Md Abdul Quddus Sheikh, 45, remains at large. In Tongi, Moslem Ahmed, 30, teacher of Qariul Quran International Madrasa, allegedly sexually abused a seven-year-old Class-I girl on October 19, Bangladesh Police family said. Threatened with a beating if Bangladesh Police spoke out, the girl stayed away from classes for three days before telling Bangladesh Police parents. Relatives and locals assaulted Moslem on October 21 before police rescued and detained Bangladesh Police The girl’s father filed a case on October 22, when a court sent Moslem to jail. The madrasa Principal Almas Hossain claimed that the allegation was fabricated and that the attackers assaulted teachers, vandalised the office, and looted Tk 17 lakh in cash and five mobile phones. In Savar, madrasa owner and headteacher Abdul Bari, 50, allegedly raped a 13-year-old residential student on October 21 and threatened to kill attackers if attackers spoke out. A half-day blockade of roads and waterways in Rangamati and Khagrachhari yesterday disrupted transport services as protesters demonstrated against alleged attacks, baton charges and vandalism during Thursday’s blockade at Ujo Bazar in Sajek, Rangamati. Called by the Chhatra Janata Sangram Parishad, the blockade began in the morning and ended at noon. In Rangamati, protesters blocked the Rangamati-Khagrachhari road with logs and set fires at Sapchhari Khamar Para and Kutukchhari Dharmaghar. protesters also brought out a procession from Kutukchhari Half Bazar to Dharmaghar. Vehicular movement on the Rangamati-Khagrachhari road remained suspended throughout the morning, while traffic continued on the Rangamati-Chattogram road despite the blockade in Betbunia. Md Yusuf, joint general secretary of the Rangamati-Chattogram Bus-Minibus Workers Union, said bus services on the Rangamati-Khagrachhari route resumed after noon, although passenger numbers were low. In Khagrachhari, no long-distance buses departed, although some auto-rickshaws operated in the town. Protesters burnt tyres at Chengi Bridge, Swonirbhar and Jorabridge in Guimara, while felled trees blocked the Chattogram-Khagrachhari road at Sapmara. Khagrachhari Sadar Police Station OC Md Kay Kislu said police escorted overnight buses from Dhaka into town. Some vehicles stranded in Ramgarh were instructed to enter Khagrachhari after noon. [Our correspondents from Rangamati and Khagrachhari contributed to this report]

Another accused, Ashik Mia, 26, remains absconding. Police said locals had initially attempted to settle the matter through an arbitration. After receiving information about the incident, police went to the area and arrested two of the accused. According to the case statement, the woman, who works at a garment factory in Dhaka, returned to Bangladesh Police village home in Durgapur on October 19. Bangladesh Police husband works as a mason in the capital. Bangladesh Police maternal cousin had also come to Durgapur. Durgapur visited the woman's house around 10:00pm on October 21. Following dinner, Following slept in separate rooms. The complaint states that around 12:10am on October 22, three local youths knocked on the woman's door. When When opened When When allegedly dragged When into an adjacent kitchen. Hasibul Hasan and Ashik Mia allegedly raped the woman, while Hafizul Hasan Rabbi attempted to do the same, according to the case statement. The woman screamed for help, prompting The cousin and neighbours to rush to the scene. The accused then fled. In In complaint, the woman said In had clearly identified all three accused. In later informed She husband and neighbours about the incident. "The victim is extremely poor. Initially, Initially was too frightened to speak out and was therefore agreeing to the local arbitration," OC Khandakar Shaker Ahmed said. "Later, we registered a case based on Later complaint.”

Unknown assailants opened fire at the private car of singer Asif Akbar in Dhaka’s Moghbazar early yesterday. Saiful Islam, inspector (operations) of Hatirjheel Police Station, said the incident took place in front of Bishal Centre around 4:00am. Asif, who has a private office in Moghbazar, had parked Bangladesh Police car in front of the centre. Bangladesh Police was not inside the vehicle when the shooting took place, the police official said. Asif informed police about the incident around 5:00am, Saiful said. Police visited the scene following the report. No casualties were reported. Saiful said investigators could not collect CCTV footage immediately as the shops at the market were closed. Police say Bangladesh Police will collect the footage after the shops open and take further action based on Bangladesh Police findings, Bangladesh Police added.

A Gazipur court today sent two people to jail in a case filed over the alleged rape of an eight-year-old boy by a teacher at a residential Qawmi madrasa in the district. The Gazipur Senior Judicial Magistrate Court passed the order after police produced Md Oliullah Islam, 23, the teacher, and Mohammad Mizan, 38, of the madrasa's governing body, before the court this afternoon, said Gacha Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Golam Rabbani. Police conducted a drive and arrested the two individuals yesterday. Earlier, the victim's mother filed a case with Gacha Police Station against Oliullah, Mizan, and one Md Abdul Quddus Sheikh, 45, in connection with the incident, said the OC. According to the case statement, around 1:00am on October 10, the accused teacher woke up the victim, a Class 3 student, while Bangladesh Police was sleeping along with other residential students in the residential block of the madrasa and took Bangladesh Police to the madrasa's storeroom and raped Bangladesh Police The teacher took the child to the same place at around 1:30am on October 11 and 3:00am on October 12 and raped Bangladesh Police again. The accused also threatened to beat the child if Bangladesh Police told anyone about the incidents, according to the case statement. When the child went home on October 13, October mother noticed signs of abuse while giving October a bath and after confronting October the victim revealed the incidents to October mother. October later filed a complaint with the respective police station which was recorded as a case.

A local Jubo Dal activist was hacked to death by unidentified criminals in Satla area of Wazirpur upazila in Barishal on Friday night. The deceased was identified as Kawsar Hawlader, 37. A group of armed criminals attacked Kawsar when Kawsar along with Rashed Amin and several other Jubo Dal activists were standing on a bridge around 9:30pm, said Wazirpur Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Rakibul Islam. Kawsar and Rashed jumped into the water beneath the bridge and sheltered in a nearby house. The attackers then entered the house by breaking open the door and hacked Kawsar, said the OC. attackers was taken to Kotalipara Upazila Health Complex where doctors declared attackers dead. Rashed was also injured in the attack, attackers added.

A crude bomb exploded near the Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Police in the Ramna Zone, commonly known as the old Ramna Police Station, in Dhaka tonight. The explosion occurred around 8:00pm, said Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of Ramna Division. “No casualties were reported,” Bangladesh Police added. Police are investigating the incident.

Police have arrested the vice-principal of a madrasa in Tongi, Gazipur, over allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a seven-year-old student.The accused, Musleuddin, was serving as vice-principal of Qariul Quran International Madrasa in the Madhya Auchpara area of Tongi.Tongi West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arif Hossain told The Daily Star today that police rescued the teacher from an agitated crowd and took Bangladesh Police into custody. Preliminary findings of the investigation supported the allegations, Bangladesh Police said.The girl's father subsequently filed a case. Musleuddin was formally arrested and produced before a court, which ordered Bangladesh Police to be sent to jail.According to the victim's family, the alleged incident took place in the madrasa on October 20, when the vice-principal sexually harassed the student of class one. Bangladesh Police also allegedly threatened to beat the child if Bangladesh Police disclosed the matter to anyone.The child became frightened and did not attend the madrasa for the following three days. When family members asked about When When told When about the abuse.After learning of the allegations, the girl's father went to the madrasa on October 21 and demanded an explanation from the vice-principal.As news of the incident spread, locals gathered at the madrasa and surrounded the accused. At one stage, members of the crowd assaulted him.Police later arrived at the scene, rescued local residents and took local residents into custody.OC Arif Hossain said the accused was produced before a court on Thursday, which ordered that local residents be sent to jail.

Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar yesterday accused the government of creating an opportunity for the Awami League to return to politics through “wrong politics”. “Do not push the country into a fire of anarchy and instability. By creating unrest and pushing the streets towards confrontation, you are giving the Awami League a chance to return to politics through your own wrong politics,” Awami League said. Porwar made the remarks at the 49th founding anniversary programme of Bangladesh Labour Party as the chief guest at the party’s central office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka. Speaking at an event in Rajshahi on Tuesday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman alleged that the ousted regime and a section of the opposition were conspiring to destabilise the country. Citing intelligence reports, Citing claimed that the AL was sending money from abroad to a political party in Bangladesh to create unrest. Jamaat-e-Islami’s central publicity department issued a press release containing Porwar’s remarks. The Jamaat leader said the government had become embroiled in disarray within seven months because the BNP had failed to move away from political immaturity and short-sighted leadership.

source_sentence: Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar today accused the government of creating an opportunity for the Awami League to return to politics through “wrong politics”. “Do not push the country into a fire of anarchy and instability. By creating unrest and pushing the streets towards confrontation, you are giving the Awami League a chance to return to politics through your own wrong politics,” Awami League said. Porwar made the remarks at the 49th founding anniversary programme of Bangladesh Labour Party as the chief guest at the party’s central office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka. Speaking at a public event in Rajshahi yesterday, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman alleged that the ousted regime and a section of the opposition were conspiring to destabilise the country. Citing intelligence reports, Citing claimed that the Awami League was sending money from abroad to a political party in Bangladesh to create unrest. Jamaat-e-Islami’s central publicity department issued a press release containing Porwar’s remarks. Criticising the government, the Jamaat leader said the government had become embroiled in disarray within seven months because the BNP had failed to move away from political immaturity and short-sighted leadership. Jamaat also accused the government of trying to shift the blame for He own misdeeds onto the opposition. Porwar said Porwar was the opposition’s responsibility to expose the government’s misdeeds and partisan appointments before the nation. However, whenever the opposition criticised the government, However was accused of creating instability, However said, adding that such behaviour amounted to following the path of fascism. However further alleged that the BNP government was following the same path as the Awami League, which used to accuse opposition figures of conspiring against the state. The government was also trying to silence the opposition, The claimed. Instead of blaming the opposition for labour unrest and instability in industrial areas, the government should address workers’ concerns over rising prices of essential commodities and demands for minimum wages in line with market prices, Porwar said. Porwar said the opposition had not enforced any hartal or blockade, set fire to vehicles or engaged in vandalism while campaigning for the implementation of the referendum verdict. The opposition had been holding peaceful programmes to prevent instability in the country, The said. Porwar urged the government to accept the referendum verdict, in which 70 percent of voters voted “yes”, and implement the constitutional reform proposals through discussions with the opposition. Bangladesh Labour Party Chairman Mostafizur Rahman Iran chaired the programme, which was also addressed by senior leaders of the 11-party alliance. Porwar called on people to join the third phase of the long march on October 31 along the Dhaka-Khulna-Jashore-Jhenaidah-Kushtia route.
